metadata.title: Implement Form Type Detection for Workspace Onboarding Edit View

objective.summary: Implement the ability to detect and display the appropriate onboarding form (Quick Start vs Complex) when users edit an existing workspace based on the new 'formType' field from the backend.
objective.background:
The backend now includes a 'formType' field ('quick' | 'complex') in workspace.onboarding.meta that indicates which onboarding form was originally used when creating the workspace. This flag persists permanently and allows the frontend to show the same form type during editing.
Previously, the system could not reliably determine which form to show during editing because the completionLevel field recalculates based on filled fields. Now, formType provides an explicit, persistent indicator of user preference.
objective.success_criteria: - When editing a workspace, the correct form (Quick or Complex) is displayed based on formType - Users can switch between Quick and Complex forms if desired - New workspaces send formType during creation - Legacy workspaces (without formType) are handled gracefully with fallback logic - All workspace edit flows preserve or update formType appropriately

change.description: Response now includes formType in onboarding.meta
change.notes: - formType is ALWAYS present (backend ensures it for legacy workspaces) - For legacy workspaces: formType is derived from completionLevel ('quick_start' → 'quick', else 'complex') - formType values: 'quick' | 'complex'

change.description: Can now accept formType in onboarding payload
change.notes: - formType is OPTIONAL in request - If not provided, backend derives it from completionLevel - Frontend SHOULD send formType to explicitly indicate which form was shown

change.description: Can now accept formType to switch between form types
change.request_example:
<!-- Scenario 1: Update fields without changing form type -->
{
  "goal": { "primaryGoal": "generate_leads" }
  <!-- formType not sent → original formType is preserved -->
}

<!-- Scenario 2: Switch from Quick to Complex form -->
{
  "formType": "complex",  <!-- Explicitly switch form type -->
  "goal": {
    "primaryGoal": "grow_audience",
    "expectedOutcome": "Get 10k followers in 6 months"
  },
  "audience": {
    "audienceType": "founders",
    "awarenessLevel": "beginner"
  }
}

<!-- Scenario 3: Switch from Complex to Quick form -->
{
  "formType": "quick",  <!-- Explicitly switch form type -->
  "goal": { "primaryGoal": "grow_audience" },
  "audience": { "audienceType": "founders" },
  "voice": { "tones": ["casual"] },
  "contentStrategy": { "pillars": ["education"] },
  "constraints": { "platforms": ["threads"] }
}
change.notes: - formType is OPTIONAL in update request - If formType is NOT sent: backend preserves original formType - If formType IS sent: backend updates to new formType (allows switching) - Backend always preserves original formType unless explicitly changed

step.code_example:
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button' import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge' interface FormTypeToggleProps { currentType: OnboardingFormType onSwitch: (newType: OnboardingFormType) => void } export function FormTypeToggle({ currentType, onSwitch }: FormTypeToggleProps) { const isQuick = currentType === 'quick' return (
Form Type: {isQuick ? 'Quick Start' : 'Complete Setup'}

{isQuick ? 'Quick Start: Edit only essential fields (5-7 fields)' : 'Complete Setup: Edit all onboarding details for maximum personalization' }

) }

test_case.description: Edit workspace with formType='quick' shows Quick form
test_case.steps: 1. Create a workspace using Quick Start form 2. Navigate to workspace edit page 3. Verify Quick Start form is displayed by default 4. Verify only 5-7 essential fields are visible
test_case.expected_result: Quick Start form is shown with minimal fields

test_case.description: Edit workspace with formType='complex' shows Complex form
test_case.steps: 1. Create a workspace using Complete Setup form 2. Navigate to workspace edit page 3. Verify Complete Setup form is displayed by default 4. Verify all onboarding fields are visible
test_case.expected_result: Complete Setup form is shown with all fields

test_case.description: Legacy workspace without formType defaults correctly
test_case.steps: 1. Fetch a legacy workspace (created before formType feature) 2. Check if formType is present in response (backend ensures it) 3. Navigate to workspace edit page 4. Verify correct form is shown based on derived formType
test_case.expected_result: Appropriate form shown based on completionLevel fallback

test_case.description: Updating workspace without changing formType preserves it
test_case.steps: 1. Open workspace with formType='quick' 2. Edit a field (e.g., change primaryGoal) 3. Save without changing formType 4. Reload workspace 5. Verify formType is still 'quick'

test_case.description: Switching from Quick to Complex works
test_case.steps: 1. Open workspace with formType='quick' 2. Click "Switch to Complete Form" button 3. Verify Complex form is now displayed 4. Fill in additional complex fields 5. Save with formType='complex' in payload 6. Reload workspace 7. Verify formType is now 'complex'
test_case.expected_result: Form type switches and persists correctly

test_case.description: Switching from Complex to Quick shows warning
test_case.steps: 1. Open workspace with formType='complex' and complex fields filled 2. Click "Switch to Quick Form" button 3. Verify warning dialog appears about hidden fields 4. Confirm switch 5. Verify Quick form is now displayed 6. Save with formType='quick' in payload 7. Reload workspace 8. Verify formType is now 'quick' but complex data still exists
test_case.expected_result: Warning shown, form switches, data preserved but hidden

test_case.steps: 1. Create workspace using Quick Start form 2. Inspect network request payload 3. Verify formType='quick' is included 4. Create workspace using Complete Setup form 5. Inspect network request payload 6. Verify formType='complex' is included
test_case.expected_result: formType is sent in creation request

test_case.description: Visual indicators show current form type
test_case.steps: 1. Open workspace edit page 2. Verify badge/indicator shows current form type 3. Verify descriptive text explains current form 4. Switch form types 5. Verify indicator updates accordingly
test_case.expected_result: Clear visual feedback about current form type

notes.note: The backend ALWAYS returns formType (it ensures it exists for legacy workspaces), so frontend should treat formType as always present in the response.
When updating onboarding, formType should ONLY be included in the request if the user explicitly switched form types. This allows the backend to preserve the original formType.
Consider adding analytics tracking for: - How often users switch between form types - Which form type is more commonly used - Whether users who start with Quick eventually switch to Complex
The form type switch feature is optional. If it adds complexity, you can start with just detecting and showing the appropriate form, without allowing switching.
When switching from Complex to Quick, do NOT delete the complex field data. Just hide it. The backend preserves all data even when formType changes.
